data.title: engine-reference honours definedness: undefined reads are typed outcomes on every checking and emission path

data.body:
[risk:high] Nested definedness guards are skipped, allowing false verdicts and certificates.

`Definedness::of` accepts `I#defined#defined` as the guard of `I#defined` at `crates/continuum-model-core/src/definedness.rs:117-135`. This scan evaluates only `guard_of(I)` and then `I`. It never checks the guard of that guard. `ModelBuilder` accepts `#`, and the programmatic model API remains supported. A model with `I = true`, `I#defined = true`, and `I#defined#defined = false` therefore reports `Holds`. The same gap reaches liveness and `emit_invariant_closure` through `crates/continuum-engine-reference/src/certificate.rs:895-903`. The kernel can verify the emitted constant-true invariant. Action chains similarly bypass finite-closure refusal.

Failure modes: silent Established, liveness Holds, admissible predicate witnesses, and Verified certificates over an undefined guard.
Edge cases: action and invariant chains, deeper suffix chains, and nested-guard evaluation errors. Ordinary CML guards remain total.
Rollback: reject nested guards or revert this feature until the scanner follows the full guard chain.
Monitoring: add a refusal counter and regression cases. Current outputs do not expose skipped nested guards.
Validation: cover checking, deadlock, liveness, witnesses, and both emitters with false and failing nested guards.

Make guard evaluation recursive, or fail closed on any nested definedness predicate.

data.reason: [risk:high] The scanner skips nested definedness guards. A supported programmatic model can therefore produce false Holds or Verified certificate results. See the open file-and-line finding.

data.body: Verified at 5aec4627: guards_of and action_chains now evaluate each complete chain deepest first. Checking, liveness, witnesses, and both emitters use the repaired scan. The original nested-guard bypass is fixed.

data.reason: Fixed by complete deepest-first chain evaluation at target 5aec4627.

data.body:
[risk:high] An action that shares the full name of a definedness-chain member is misclassified as predicate-only, so global undefined-read scans can skip it.

At crates/continuum-model-core/src/definedness.rs:183-189, the classifier checks only stripped prefixes against action_names. It never checks the current predicate name. ModelBuilder validates action and predicate namespaces separately, so a supported programmatic model can declare action I#defined and predicates I plus I#defined, or collide at any deeper member. The chain remains well_formed and becomes Guarded::Predicate(I), not Guarded::Action. The false member is then absent from action_chains. Checks of unrelated predicates and deadlock can report success, and crates/continuum-engine-reference/src/certificate.rs:890-903 can emit a finite-closure certificate that the kernel verifies because the kernel does not read definedness predicates.

Failure modes: silent Holds or deadlock success for unrelated obligations, plus a Verified finite-closure certificate over a model the stated fail-closed rule marks undefined.
Edge cases: collisions at the shallowest or deeper member, exact action names, and action-instance schemas such as I#defined(k=0).
Rollback: reject cross-namespace chain-member collisions, or revert nested-chain classification until every member name is checked.
Monitoring: count and surface ambiguous action/predicate chain classifications before checking or emission.
Validation: add exact-name and schema-name collision cases for checking, deadlock, liveness, witnesses, and both emitters. Assert that finite closure is refused.

Include the full member name in the action collision test before accepting a chain as predicate-guarding.

data.reason: High blocker: Definedness::of omits the full chain-member name from action collision checks. A same-named action and predicate is misclassified as predicate-only, allowing unrelated checks and finite-closure emission to skip a false definedness guard.
